summary: Iteration 4 backend testing complete for Panda Chat (rebranded from Omega Chat). All 80 pytest tests pass — 65 regression (test_api.py 19, test_iteration2.py 15, test_iteration3.py 29, test_ws.py 2) plus 15 new iter-4 tests covering the 'document' message type. New coverage: (1) POST /api/conversations/{id}/messages with type=document returns full Message with filename/filesize/media_mime/media_base64 echoed back plus message_id/conversation_id/sender_id/created_at/read_at=null; MongoDB _id not leaked. (2) Sending a document updates last_message to '📎 <filename>' and last_message_type='document' in GET /api/conversations. (3) GET /api/conversations/{id}/messages returns document messages with all fields (filename, filesize, media_mime, media_base64) intact. (4) Sending document without media_base64 returns 400 with 'media' in detail. (5) Sending document without filename falls back to '📎 File' preview. (6) Pydantic Literal validation returns 422 for unknown types ('audio', 'sticker', 'gif', 'location', ''). (7) Regression: text preview keeps trimmed text, image → '📷 Photo', video → '🎥 Video', image without media still 400. (8) Regression: mark-read cycles preserve filename/filesize/media_mime/media_base64 on document messages; read_at properly populated across multiple send+read cycles. Backend server.py is clean, uses Literal['text','image','video','document'] on both MessageCreate and Message models.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py MessageCreate.type and Message.type both use Literal['text','image','video','document'] — pydantic will correctly emit 422 for any other value. Verified.

send_message preview logic: text→trimmed text[:120], image→'📷 Photo', video→'🎥 Video', else→'📎 <filename or File>'. Because the else branch fires for anything non-text/image/video and only 'document' is allowed by the Literal, the '📎' preview is document-specific. Correct.
Missing-media check runs before preview computation for all non-text types (image, video, document) — 400 is consistent across binary types.

filename/filesize are Optional[str]/Optional[int] on both Message and MessageCreate; nothing enforces non-empty filename or positive filesize on the server. This is fine per spec (client validates), but could be tightened later.
server.py still uses deprecated @app.on_event startup/shutdown handlers (carried over from iter 1–3). Non-blocking.
No max-size guard on media_base64 — a large PDF could balloon Mongo doc size. Consider a size cap or streaming/S3 offload for production. Non-blocking for MVP.
